_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every upstream pin this repo depends on.
Nothing else in the tree may DECLARE a pin value. package.json and package-lock.json
files CONTAIN pin values, but they are derived: `tools/repin.py --check` fails if any of
them disagrees with this file, and `tools/repin.py --apply` rewrites them from it.
Prose that mentions a version must mention one of the versions declared here; the same
check enforces that, so a stale number in a README fails rather than misleads.
Verified by verification/verify_pinned_nightly_single_source.sh.
The re-pin POLICY (when to bump, what a bump must record) is PINS.md.

interchangeable. `current` is THE pin: new work uses it. `deletion_era` is frozen
evidence — the published line whose src/public tree is byte-comparable with the `ts`
anchor, which is what lets the deleted TS AVM run at all, and which still ships the
in-process NAPI AVM the differential oracle needs. Bumping `deletion_era` would destroy
the artefact rather than update it.

_comment: THE LIVE CHAIN THE REPLAY CAMPAIGN (Aztec-Live-Chain-Replay.milestones.org) TALKS TO, and
the protocol version its node client checks a node against. L0's deliverable is 'the node's
protocol version checked against pins.json and a mismatch reported loudly'; this is the
declaration that check reads.
THE NETWORK IS NOT PINNED, AND THAT SENTENCE HAS CHANGED ITS REASON. L0's implementation
probed five candidate endpoints on 2026-08-29 and recorded that every one of them failed;
the transcript is still in `probed_endpoints` below and every one of those five still fails.
L0's REVIEW re-took the search on the same day and found TWO THAT ANSWER — dRPC's Aztec
mainnet and Aztec testnet endpoints, both running nodeVersion 5.2.0, both answering a real
`aztec_getNodeInfo`, and both advertising `x-aztec-l2circuitsvktreeroot` and
`x-aztec-l2protocolcontractshash` EQUAL TO THE TWO VALUES PINNED BELOW. So the protocol pin
is validated against a live chain rather than against the packages alone, and the campaign's
open question 'Mainnet has not been verified to exist for Aztec' is answered: it exists,
l1ChainId 1, rollup 0x91ff8bbd8ebb07893010d50a48a1609e5ebd8e34.
WHY `network` IS STILL UNESTABLISHED AND `rpc_url` IS STILL NULL, WHICH IS A SECOND
MEASUREMENT AND NOT INERTIA. Both reachable endpoints are PROXIES, and a proxy is measured
here rather than assumed: a single-object JSON-RPC POST comes back WITH the `x-aztec-*`
headers and a BATCH (array) POST comes back WITHOUT them. Upstream's own
`createAztecNodeClient` always batches (`sendBatch`, `batchWindowMS = 0`), so through these
endpoints upstream's versioning handler never sees a header, and `assertProtocolVersion`
refuses them naming the absence — which is the SAFE direction and the behaviour L0 designed,
but it means a pinned `rpc_url` pointing at a proxy would be an endpoint this repository's own
version check cannot verify. Pinning the network needs a DIRECT node endpoint, or a
deliberately un-batched version probe. That was offered to L1 as its first task and L1 DID
NOT TAKE IT, deliberately: no direct (non-proxying) Aztec endpoint was found, and the
alternative — an un-batched version probe issued by the client — is a SECOND WAY OF TALKING
TO A NODE, which is the kind of second wire path L0's whole 'nothing here declares a schema'
deliverable exists to prevent. So `network` stays UNESTABLISHED, and every L1 fixture records
the header absence AS WHAT THE CLIENT SAW, beside an un-batched probe explicitly labelled a
reconstruction. See `captured_fixtures.version_headers_note`.
WHAT IS PINNED IS THE PROTOCOL-LEVEL HALF, AND UPSTREAM PINS EXACTLY THAT HALF THE SAME WAY.
`yarn-project/aztec/src/cli/versioning.ts` at the `cpp` anchor returns, when it has no chain
config, `{ l2CircuitsVkTreeRoot: getVKTreeRoot().toString(), l2ProtocolContractsHash:
protocolContractsHash.toString() }` — a PARTIAL ComponentsVersions with the two fields that
are a property of the protocol rather than of a deployment. `validatePartialComponentVersions
Match` and `getVersioningResponseHandler` both ignore undefined fields, so a partial is
upstream's own supported shape and not a weakening we invented.
Both values are DERIVED, from the packages `npm.current` names, and both are re-derived by
`verify_client_uses_upstream_schema` on every run rather than trusted here: a figure nobody
re-derives rots. If a bump moves either, that check goes red before anything ships.

_comment: THE STATED CONSEQUENCE OF A PARTIAL PIN, TAKEN AS A MEASUREMENT ON 2026-08-29 RATHER THAN
ARGUED. `pinned_protocol_version.ts` says 'a node on the WRONG L1 CHAIN would not be caught by
this pin today, and a node running a DIFFERENT PROTOCOL would be'. Aztec mainnet and Aztec
testnet were both read on the same day: their two PROTOCOL-level headers are IDENTICAL to each
other and to the pin, and their three NETWORK-level headers all differ. So the first half of
that sentence is demonstrated — today's pin genuinely cannot tell mainnet from testnet — and
the second half is the reason the pin is worth having at all.
L1's committed recordings of this chain. The FILES are the record and these entries are an
index into them: every one of them carries its own full provenance block, and
`e2e_fetch_settled_transaction` re-derives the coordinates below from the recorded
RESPONSES rather than reading them back out of the provenance, so the two can disagree.
BOTH OF L1'S ARE TESTNET, AND THAT WAS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE. Aztec
mainnet answered and was COMPLETELY IDLE. Two independent sightings on 2026-08-29: 150
consecutive blocks (64395-64544) with zero transactions, and — re-taken by L1's review at
tip 64571 — 200 consecutive blocks (64372-64571) with zero transactions.
THAT SENTENCE IS NO LONGER TRUE, AND L2 RE-TOOK IT RATHER THAN INHERITING IT.
On 2026-08-30 MAINNET CARRIES REAL TRANSACTIONS. Scanning 66150-66290 (141 blocks, 3
unanswered) found two: block 66214, tx
nullifiers, 1 public log, 2 public data writes — and block 66217, tx
nullifiers, 1 public data write. Both revertCode 0. So the campaign's second standing
chain fact is RETIRED: there IS something on mainnet to capture.
AND MAINNET IS STILL NOT A DEMO SOURCE, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT SENTENCE AND THE USEFUL ONE.
Two transactions in 141 blocks is roughly one per seventy, and the replayability window is
the finality lag below — 38 blocks when this was taken. A scan of the whole replayable
window 66250-66292 found ZERO transactions. So a mainnet transaction is typically ALREADY
PRUNED by the time anything notices it, and a mainnet demo would need a FOLLOWER catching
transactions as they appear, not a scan finding them afterwards.
TESTNET, MEANWHILE, HAS A HEARTBEAT, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES A DEMO POSSIBLE AT ALL.
One transaction every ELEVEN blocks, almost exactly — 62507, 62518, 62529, 62540, 62551,
1 nullifier and 9 public data writes, against the same contract
0x2a9a1d0e8f1974267536abefa565e7a7351f92ddbe95ec13c57c79b70664f7c8 with the same 23,157
bytes of packed bytecode as L1's fixture. Eleven blocks is about thirteen minutes, and the
window is about twenty-nine blocks, so THERE ARE ALWAYS TWO OR THREE REPLAYABLE
TRANSACTIONS. The practical consequence is the opposite of L1's: L1's fixtures could never
be re-captured, and an L2 fixture over this heartbeat CAN be, on demand, within minutes.
That is the difference between a demo and a museum piece, and it is a property of a bot
somebody else is running, so it is recorded with a date and re-taken rather than relied on.
AND THE CAPTURE HAS A DEADLINE, WHICH NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY HAD RECORDED.
`getTxByHash` PRUNES AND `getTxEffect` DOES NOT, so a settled transaction can become
UNREPLAYABLE WHILE REMAINING PERFECTLY VISIBLE: the node keeps EFFECTS indefinitely and
TRANSACTION BODIES for a window, and a replay needs the body — it is what
`AvmTxHint.fromTx` consumes.
THE WINDOW IS NOT A BLOCK COUNT AND IT IS NOT ~36. L1's implementation measured two
sightings (at tip 60605 the oldest fetchable was 60570, 35 back; at tip 60620 it was
60583, 37 back) and generalised them to 'roughly 36 blocks'. L1's REVIEW re-took the
measurement four hours later and got 54-65 blocks, then established the MECHANISM in
upstream's own source at `anchors.cpp` rather than curve-fitting the sightings:
* `AztecNodeService.getTxByHash` (yarn-project/aztec-node/src/aztec-node/server.ts:637)
calls `p2pClient.getTxByHashFromPool` and NOTHING ELSE. It never consults the tx
ARCHIVE — that is a separate method, `getArchivedTxByHash`, which the node does not
expose, and `archivedTxLimit` (P2P_ARCHIVED_TX_LIMIT) defaults to 0 anyway.
* The pool deletes a mined tx when its block is FINALIZED:
`tx_pool_v2_impl.ts#prepareFinalization` takes the finalized block as the cutoff and
`findTxsMinedAtOrBefore(cutoff)` names every tx to delete. `keepFinalizedTxsForSlots`
(P2P_KEEP_FINALIZED_TXS_FOR_SLOTS) defaults to 0, i.e. delete at the finalized tip.
So the horizon is `getBlockNumber() - getBlockNumber('finalized')`: A FINALITY LAG, fixed
in TIME and therefore variable in BLOCKS with whatever rate the chain is producing them.
Measured by the review at 2026-08-29T03:02Z: tip 60659, finalized 60601 (58 blocks, and
3,096 seconds ~ 52 minutes of block timestamps); oldest fetchable block-with-a-tx 60605,
newest pruned 60594, which brackets the predicted boundary of finalized+1 = 60602. Ten
minutes later the same gap read 65 blocks because the tip advanced and `finalized` had
not yet moved.
THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT BOUNDS THE PRODUCT: a demo over 'recent
Aztec transactions' has a replayability window of ROUGHLY AN HOUR, not a fixed number of
blocks, and a demo left alone silently degrades from debuggable to merely visible. It does
not have to be guessed at: `getBlockNumber` is ALREADY on the permitted surface and takes
a tag, so `getBlockNumber('finalized')` reads the horizon at run time with no widening of
the fourteen. Anything at or below that block is already unfetchable.
This is a property of the node's retention configuration and not of the protocol, it is
why `just capture-replay-fixture` is a deliberate act and not part of `verify-l1`, and it
is why an old transaction cannot be re-captured at all.

Its eighth recorded call is `aztec_getContract ["0x2a9a1d0e...", 62639]` - the settling block ON THE WIRE, which L1's two recordings deliberately do not have and cannot be given, because adding the argument to an existing recording turns every one of its calls into a FixtureMiss and L1's transactions can no longer be re-captured. fixtures.regenerable: REGENERABLE, AND THE WIRING WAS MISSING UNTIL IT WAS CHECKED. `just capture-replay-fixture pin=1`. The `pin` parameter did not exist when this file was first captured, so the fixture was frozen by an accident of the CLI rather than by the retention horizon — which is the only reason a fixture here is allowed to be frozen. Proven on 2026-08-30 by regenerating to a scratch path: a fresh transaction in block 62672, with `aztec_getContract ["0x2a9a1d0e...", 62672]` on the wire and the fabricated probe recorded both ways.

fixtures.for: L2'S OWN FIXTURE, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF RECORDING FROM L1'S. L1's capture recorded the calls fetchSettledTransaction makes, which are known in advance. L2's HYDRATION CALLS ARE NOT KNOWN IN ADVANCE - the AVM discovers them, round by round, by reporting the world-state queries it made - so the only list that can be right is the one produced by RUNNING THE REPLAY against a live node. That is what this file is: the fetch's own calls plus the per-slot aztec_getPublicDataWitness / aztec_getNullifierMembershipWitness reads at block 62638, every one of them a call the replay itself made. Both witness methods were already on L0's permitted fourteen and are members of the MembershipWitnessSource seam L0 declared for exactly this, so L2 widened nothing.

replay_result.comparisons: 23 matched, 0 mismatched - revertCode, transactionFee, all 9 publicDataWrites (leafSlot AND value), and the single nullifier
replay_result.gas: the AVM's publicGas l2Gas 290,431 plus the private kernel's 590,800 is 881,231, which is block 62639's own totalManaUsed; daGas 512 + 128 = 640
replay_result.tree_roots: ALL FOUR DIFFER FROM THE BLOCK'S STATE REFERENCE, BY CONSTRUCTION AND NOT BY ERROR. See replay/src/replay_execution.ts TREE_ROOTS_DIVERGE_REASON: the values the transaction read are the chain's, fetched per-slot at the parent block; the membership proofs around them are the resident tree's. A recording that carried the chain's state reference beside this execution would be a wrong root that everything downstream believes.

fixtures.regenerable: REGENERABLE. `just capture-replay-run`, which drives the REAL replay against a live node and records every call it makes — including the wrong-block control's second pass. It has to be that: L2's hydration calls are discovered by the AVM at run time, so a hand-listed capture would be a guess about what the check will ask for.

captured_fixtures.version_headers_note: Each fixture records the `x-aztec-*` headers TWICE: `onBatchPost` is what upstream's client saw (EMPTY, because this endpoint proxies and strips them on the array POST upstream always sends) and `onSingleObjectPost` is a deliberately un-batched probe taken in the same run. The second is labelled a RECONSTRUCTION inside the file. Playing back the first reproduces the live `assertProtocolVersion` refusal offline; the second is what says the obstacle is the proxy and not this repository's version check. A fixture that silently stored the second would be kinder than the chain it came from.
captured_fixtures.regeneration_note: A FIXTURE THAT CAN BE REGENERATED IS WORTH MORE THAN ONE THAT CANNOT — BUT ONLY IF REGENERATING IT IS ACTUALLY WIRED UP. `l1_prepare` now asserts, for every declared fixture, that `provenance.capturedBy` names a script that exists and is TRACKED, so the wiring is checked offline rather than described. What it deliberately does NOT assert is that re-running the script reproduces the file: against a live chain it never could, and for L1's two the transactions are gone, so the honest claim is that the path exists and is committed.

npm_exceptions._comment: @aztec-scoped packages that are NOT on the nightly line and must not be moved onto it. Each needs a reason; the check refuses any other exception.

@aztec/viem.why: A fork of viem republished under the @aztec scope, aliased in as `viem`. It follows viem's own versioning, not the monorepo nightly line, and no nightly of it exists.

@aztec/merkle-tree.why: The deleted TypeScript merkle trees (REUSE-INVENTORY.md RI-28). Upstream removed the package in e264dd4893 (2026-03-16), so this is the LAST nightly that ships it and no later one exists. Consumed only by probe-mt/, the probe that measured the undomained-hash defect. Pinning it forward is impossible, not merely undesirable.

npm_pin_witnesses._comment: Tracked files that carry an npm version literal as part of what they ARE, rather than as a dependency declaration. Two kinds. A MEASURED ARTEFACT records which pin it was produced against; if the literal drifts, the artefact has silently stopped describing the tree it was measured on. SOURCE THAT PUBLISHES THE PIN states it as behaviour: orchestration/src/disclosure.ts puts it in the runtime's own section-8.4 disclosure line, so a stale literal there is a false statement made to a user rather than a stale comment. Neither kind is a package file, so neither is a consumer. Each entry maps a tracked path to the npm pin its literal must equal. `tools/repin.py` and `verify_pinned_nightly_single_source` both allow these paths AND check the agreement; neither merely exempts them.

npm_consumers._comment: Which declared npm pin each package.json/package-lock.json tree must use. Every @aztec/* dependency in these trees is checked against it.

toolchain._comment: Not upstream-Aztec pins, but pinned all the same; recorded here so there is one place to look. The authoritative declaration for each is the file named.

nim.why_here_and_not_a_flake: SUPERSEDED, and the correction is recorded rather than overwritten. This field used to say that no nixpkgs attribute named the Nim compiler this workspace uses, so `ct-writer/build.rs` took `nim` from PATH and refused a version that did not match. THAT WAS THE DEFECT, not the remedy: an agent's own shell inherits the WORKSPACE's .envrc and has nim on PATH, while `direnv exec <this repo>` -- the shell the sweep and every CI job use -- replaces PATH entirely and does not. The same check therefore passed by hand and died in the sweep, and M41's first sweep lost three of its seven checks to exactly that, with `nim is required` in the log. M19's wasm-opt finding and M25's system-node finding are the same defect; this is its third instance. `nim` is in flake.nix now, so the version is nixpkgs' as this repository's own flake.lock pins it, and this entry RECORDS that version rather than declaring it. build.rs still refuses a mismatch, which is now a guard against a shell nobody meant to be in rather than the pin itself. Everything else the Path B build needs -- clang, llvm-ar, lld, the wasi-libc headers and the zstd source -- is resolved with `nix build --inputs-from <repo>`, which pins against the same flake.lock rather than the invoking user's flake registry; measured, the two resolve different clang store paths on this host.

Crates that carry a rust-toolchain.toml -- the Noir trees and avm-transpiler -- are held to THAT file's channel by the same function instead, because forcing this pin on them would change which compiler built their artefacts.
rust.why_pinned: These builds used to install `stable`, which FLOATS. On 2026-09-28 `stable` moved 1.98.1 -> 1.99.0 and the shipped ct-writer module went from 743,420 to 744,237 bytes with no source change, breaking the figures TRACE-ABI.md section 7, WRITER-SEAM.md and JOIN-SHAPE.md quote and the checks re-derive. Every documented figure was produced with 1.98.1, so that is the pin. Moving it is a re-pin under PINS.md: rebuild, re-derive every module figure, record the before/after here and in history.

history.reason: L1's deliverable is 'fixtures captured from a live chain and committed, so the suite runs without a network, with the capture script committed beside them', and the campaign's standing instruction is to record provenance per fixture — endpoint, block, transaction, capture time, and what the node reported — because 'fabricated or unlabelled fixtures are the failure mode this campaign is built to avoid'. Each fixture file carries its own full provenance block; this entry is the index and the place two facts about the CHAIN live, neither of which belongs in a fixture: mainnet is live and completely idle (150 consecutive blocks with zero transactions on 2026-08-29, re-taken by L1's review as 200 consecutive blocks), so both fixtures are testnet by necessity rather than by preference; and `getTxByHash` prunes while `getTxEffect` does not, so a settled transaction can become unreplayable while remaining perfectly visible. The second is why the capture recipe is deliberately not part of `verify-l1`. L1's review corrected the SHAPE of that second fact: it is not a block count. The node serves a tx body only from the ACTIVE POOL, and the pool deletes a mined tx when its block is FINALIZED, so the horizon is `getBlockNumber() - getBlockNumber('finalized')` — a finality lag, fixed in time (~52 minutes measured) and variable in blocks (35-37 at L1's sightings, 54-65 at the review's four hours later). See `captured_fixtures._comment` for the upstream call chain that establishes it. The `network` field stays UNESTABLISHED and `rpc_url` stays null: L1 did not pin an endpoint, because the reason L0 recorded still holds — both reachable endpoints are proxies that strip the version headers on the batch POST upstream's client always sends, and each fixture records that emptiness as what the client actually saw.

history.reason: M37's sizing measured every upstream path PROVENANCE.md cites under yarn-project/ between the ts anchor and upstream's tip: 10 unchanged, 7 changed, 2 gone. THE TWO GONE ARE WHY THIS IS A SPLIT AND NOT A BUMP — they are the TypeScript AVM, which is the exact thing this anchor exists to preserve. But 'gone' was one word for two different facts, and re-measuring separated them: avm/avm_simulator.ts is DELETED, while avm/fixtures/utils.ts is RENAMED to avm/testing/utils.ts at 73% similarity by git's own detection, the missing 27% being precisely the five TS-AVM-dependent declarations that PROVENANCE.md's tx-builder-calldata-half class was already dropping by hand. So the frozen half is the three TREES (spike/src, diffsim/src, drift/src), which hold both files and stay here; and every single-file row moved to cpp, including the renamed one, because re-taking it with the two edits that survive there reproduces the vendored bytes EXACTLY — measured, byte-identical — so the move costs nothing and buys a row whose upstream path exists. cpp RATHER THAN A NEW ANCHOR AT UPSTREAM'S TIP, deliberately, and it is a measurement rather than a convenience: cpp (2026-08-19) is TWO commits behind origin/next (651bda5d5f, 2026-08-20) and the diff between them is three added lines of .github/workflows/aztec-cli-acceptance-test.yml — nothing under yarn-project/ or barretenberg/ at all. Every one of the nineteen paths is byte-identical at cpp and at the tip. Taking cpp therefore IS taking current upstream, and it obeys PINS.md §1's cadence instead of spending a bump on a CI workflow file. THE BEHAVIOURAL DELTA OF THE WHOLE RE-TAKE IS ZERO, and that is measured rather than hoped: the only changes inside code this repository executes are two gas constants, which upstream stopped importing from @aztec/stdlib/gas and now inlines as 98_304 and 817_500 — equal to the values orchestration/src/vendor/gas_compat.ts derived from @aztec/constants at npm.deletion_era, checked against the installed package. Everything else that changed upstream is comment text, or is inside the half the vendoring severs. The one upstream change with real semantics — insertTxEffectIntoWorldTrees taking an l1ToL2Messages parameter instead of padding txEffect.l2ToL1Msgs into the L1_TO_L2_MESSAGE_TREE — is in a function this repository never calls (a grep across the tree returns the definition and nothing else) and is recorded in DRIFT.md rather than absorbed.
